newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Two more bodies pulled from Australia landslide.
newsitem.headline: Two more bodies pulled from Australia landslide.

text.p: Rescuers looking for more survivors among the rubble of a landslide at an Australian ski resort unearthed two more bodies on Wednesday, bringing the confirmed death toll to 12.

As cloudy, windy weather closed in on the grief-stricken village of Thredbo, in the Snowy Mountains south of Sydney, rescuers pulled another two dead men from the heap of broken concrete, twisted metal, rocks, dirt and timber.
The bodies of eight men and four women have so far been recovered since a steep, heavily populated mountainside gave way late last Wednesday night, engulfing two ski lodges and burying 19 people.
On Saturday night, survivor Stuart Diver, a fit 27-year-old ski instructor, was rescued from the debris after being trapped for three freezing nights in a concrete tomb.
Police have said they have not given up hope of finding more survivors and that, in similar circumstances elsewhere around the world, victims have been known to survive up to 10 days.
Rescuers continued on Wednesday morning to prepare the dangerously unstable hillside against approaching rain, with big tarpaulins ready to be deployed over the site, police said.
If left uncovered, the hillside could give way again and flood the honeycomb of tunnels painstakingly dug by hand into the rubble in search of cavities that might hide life.

"There's always hope," police site commander Don Keene told reporters late on Tuesday. "Overseas there's been people in situations like this for 10 days, so there's hope and we just keep driving on that hope that we will be successful."
Diver is recovering in a hospital in Canberra, north of Thredbo, and is reported to be on his feet again after minor surgery for frostbite.
He was in bed with his wife, Sally, when disaster struck. Her fate is still not known.
Police have not identified any of the confirmed dead.
